decision: Which approach best resolves: WF-066 fans meeting lifecycle events out to subscriber URLs. The research quotes two payload envelopes. Chili Piper sends a flat payload with fields at the top level. Cal sends {"triggerEvent", "createdAt", "payload": {...}} for most events but a FLAT payload with no payload wrapper for MEETING_STARTED and MEETING_ENDED, and the research warns 'Do not mix them silently.' This build fires only the three Chili Piper event types (new meeting, meeting update, canceled meeting) whose documented payload fields are top level. How should the sender shape its envelope?

state.problem: WF-066 fans meeting lifecycle events out to subscriber URLs. The research quotes two payload envelopes. Chili Piper sends a flat payload with fields at the top level. Cal sends {"triggerEvent", "createdAt", "payload": {...}} for most events but a FLAT payload with no payload wrapper for MEETING_STARTED and MEETING_ENDED, and the research warns 'Do not mix them silently.' This build fires only the three Chili Piper event types (new meeting, meeting update, canceled meeting) whose documented payload fields are top level. How should the sender shape its envelope?

candidate_solutions.flat_chili_only: Send one flat Chili Piper envelope for all three event types. Document that Cal's MEETING_STARTED and MEETING_ENDED are out of scope. Never send a payload wrapper. Cost: a Cal-only subscriber cannot read these events.
candidate_solutions.reproduce_both: Send the flat Chili envelope and also implement Cal's wrapped envelope plus its two flat exceptions, keyed on a per-subscription envelope mode. Cost: three shapes in one product, and the research's warning about mixing them silently becomes a real risk.
candidate_solutions.wrapped_cal_only: Send Cal's wrapped envelope for all three event types. Cost: the three event types this workflow fires are Chili Piper's, and the research documents their fields as top level, so the documented payload contract would be wrong.

context.chili_payload_fields: meetingIdChili, title, description, location, start, end, primaryGuestTimeZone, host/assignee/booker identities and their *IdChili, primaryGuestDataFields, additionalGuests[], workspaceId/Name, productFeatureType/Name/Id, distributionName/Id, meetingTypeName/Id, type: Created|Updated|Deleted

decision: Implementation of WF-066 meets the release bar

state.change_summary:
WF-066: fan out meeting lifecycle events via signed webhooks, on branch q-ticket-3,
rebased onto origin/main at 8cf58fe.

WHAT IT IS. A feature plugin. An admin registers a subscriber URL against one of
three researched event types. A meeting created, updated or cancelled is
serialised once, signed with HMAC-SHA256 over {timestamp}.{raw_body} and hex in
X-Chili-Signature, and POSTed to every enabled subscription naming that type.
Every attempt becomes a delivery row, so a skipped subscriber is visible.

FILES ADDED, 18, none shared and none deleted.
backend/dsr/meeting_webhook_fanout/ holds eight modules: the three event types and
the payload value each fires, the signing rule, the flat payload builder, the
transport seam, the store-facing fanout, one error hierarchy, the inference
register.
backend/dsr/features/wf066_fan_out_meeting_events_via_signed_webhooks.py mounts
17 routes on /api/wf-066 and exports seed().
backend/tests/test_wf066.py and test_wf066_http.py.
frontend/src/features/wf-066-fan-out-meeting-events-via-signed-webhooks/ holds
index.jsx, MeetingWebhookFanout.jsx, api.js, primitives.jsx and a page test.
orchestration/decisions/WF-066-DESIGN.md and wf066-jev-audit.jsonl.

tools/check_feature_diff.py --base origin/main: "OK: 18 changed file(s), none
shared". git diff --name-status origin/main..HEAD reports 0 deletions. WF-060,
WF-067 and WF-070 are each byte-identical to origin/main.

MEASUREMENTS.
- Tests added: 169 backend across two files, 23 frontend page tests.
- Own files on their own: 169 passed. Under the repo addopts, the same 169.
- Whole backend suite: not re-run since the last rebase. The earlier local run
  reached 100 percent with zero failures, measured with four agents on one host.
- Coverage over the new package: TOTAL 95 percent. Per file: __init__ 100,
  errors 100, fanout 97, inferences 93, payloads 90, signing 92, transport 87,
  vocabulary 95.
- Routes: python backend/seed.py ran and printed the feature's states, including
  one delivery that failed to reach its subscriber and one event at a room whose
  subscriptions were never enabled. The return string encodes as cp1252.
  tools/verify_all_routes.py called 1237 routes across 67 features and reported
  "OK: no route returned 5xx or failed to answer", after one real defect it found
  is fixed. 46 checks driven by hand over real HTTP on port 8123 pass, including
  an independent HMAC recomputation from the published secret and raw body.
- Lint: ruff check and ruff format --check clean from the repository root with
  --config backend/pyproject.toml. Frontend eslint 0 errors and no warning in this
  folder, prettier --check clean, vite build succeeded, 491 frontend tests across
  18 files passed.

REQUIREMENTS.
- React and Tailwind UI: yes, shared primitives, semantic tokens only, min-h-11
  controls, focus rings, no emoji, every status a word beside its badge.
- Python backend: yes, discovered by the plugin host, verified through the
  registry over live HTTP.
- SQLite only through the audited wrapper: yes, and a test reads the package's
  import surface to prove no module reaches for sqlite3 or the app.
- Schema-flexible API: yes, ordinary JSON in records.data, no migration, and a
  test writes a field this build never heard of and reads it back.
- Tests present and passing: yes.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.
- The whole-suite pass and the coverage percentage were measured before the last
  two rebases. The per-package coverage above is current; the whole-suite total is
  not re-measured on this exact tree, and four agents were sharing the host.
- No browser was attached, so the page was not verified visually. It was verified
  by 23 rendered tests under jsdom and by a production vite build.
- The Jev client appends to the project's shared jev-audit.jsonl as a side effect
  of any call. This ticket writes its own record to wf066-jev-audit.jsonl and the
  shared file is left exactly as found, because four agents appending to one file
  collide on every merge.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED. verify_all_routes.py reached the one-delivery route with an
id that does not exist and got a 500. The cause was raise MeetingWebhookError(msg,
code=...): the base inherits ValueError.__init__, which takes no code keyword, so
the call raised TypeError. Fixed by a real UnknownDelivery type, and covered by
three tests including one that sweeps every unknown-id route and asserts no 5xx.

ONE DECISION A REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK. The domain package is named
dsr/meeting_webhook_fanout, not dsr/scheduling_meetings. WF-067 shipped a package
at that path in PR 215 and four file names collided. This branch moved rather than
merging into WF-067's, because WF-067's is on main and its feature module, tests
and page import those names. The two domains differ: theirs builds and tracks a
mutual action plan for e-signature approval, this one delivers meeting events
outward. Both decisions are recorded in the design document and the inference
register.

criteria.false: A shared file is edited, or the guard did not actually measure a diff

claims_backed_by_measurement.instructions: Is every claim made in the evidence supported by a measurement that was actually run, rather than asserted, read off a progress bar, or produced by a check that passed on empty input? criteria.false: A claim is asserted, or a check passed vacuously or was not run

criteria.false: A substantial part of the change was never measured, whether or not that is declared

verdict.instructions: Should this change land on main? Weigh the balance of the questions above rather than deciding on your own: where contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor are all healthy and the evidence questions show broad coverage, answer merge with the confidence that warrants. Items listed as unverified are declared context to weigh, not defects in themselves -- but a change whose coverage is genuinely thin, or which was recovered from a base far behind main and not reconciled, is fix.
